html:
A granite temple on the beach at Mamallapuram, south of Chennai in India, built by the Pallava dynasty in the early 8th century, probably under King Narasimhavarman II.

Earlier Pallava monuments at the site were cut from living rock, such as the Five Rathas. The Shore Temple is one of the first in south India to be built of cut stone blocks laid one on another, a structural temple. Its two stepped towers, one for Shiva and one smaller, set a pattern that grew into the great towers of Dravidian architecture, up to the Brihadisvara Temple of the Cholas.

Mamallapuram was a busy port then, trading across the Bay of Bengal to Southeast Asia. The sea has worn the carvings soft. The 2004 tsunami pulled the water back and briefly showed old stone ruins offshore. The temple is part of a World Heritage Site.
sum: A granite temple on the beach at Mamallapuram, south of Chennai in India, built by the Pallava dynasty in the early 8th century, probably under King Narasimhavarman II.
